UNAVOIDABLE ADVERSE ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURAL RESOURCE EFFECTS
The increase in size of catalytic converters will require an additional 2,200 troy ounces of platinum and palladium to be used. This will increase the EPA porjected use of 180,000 troy ounces in 1990 to 182,200 troy ounces. EPA concluded that their projected 180,000 troy ounces would not strain world production capabilities.
Material substitution to reduce the weight of vehicles was projected to add 10 pounds per vehicle of aluminum and 10 pounds per vehicle of plastic. The resulting total increase in aluminum and plastics would be 5.26 million pounds each. The increase in the use of aluminum is 0.055 percent of total national consumption in 1975 of 9.6 billion pounds, and the increase in the use of plastics is 0.025 percent of total national consumption in 1975 if 21.2 billion pounds. Because of the increased use of aluminum and plastics a small decrease in water quality, a small increase in industrial water supply demand, and a small increase in stationary source air pollution are likely to occur.
